From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.

# Project Kestrel: Seller Draft Review Against Buyer Playbook

**Note on currency:** The Seller's disclosure letter speaks as at 22 September 2026, and today is 5 November 2026. Confirm the status of every Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay, DD-006 and bonus item before relying on these positions.

---

### SPA-N-001: General liability cap
- **Seller:** 20% of price, AUD 4,800,000 (cl 12.1).
- **Buyer wants:** 25%, AUD 6,000,000 starting position.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the 20% cap and mark up to 25%. The 20% cap is a conditional fallback that requires prior written authority from Amelia Frost identifying the draft, and none has been given.

### SPA-N-002: De minimis and basket
- **Seller:** De minimis AUD 25,000. Basket AUD 250,000, with recovery only of the excess over the basket (cl 12.2).
- **Buyer wants:** De minimis AUD 5,000. Aggregate basket AUD 50,000, with the Seller liable from the first dollar once exceeded.
- **Recommendation:** Reject and mark up to AUD 5,000 / AUD 50,000 first-dollar. The Seller's version is five times the playbook de minimis and five times the basket, and removes first-dollar recovery.

### SPA-N-003: General claims time limit
- **Seller:** 18 months for general warranty claims. Any limitation applies to all claims unless expressly stated otherwise (cl 12.3 / 13).
- **Buyer wants:** 24 months after Completion for general claims. Any 18-month period is a fallback that needs Amelia Frost's written approval.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the 18-month period and mark up to 24 months. The "applies to all claims" wording would also pull Title and Fundamental claims into the general regime, which the playbook prohibits.

### SPA-N-004: Fundamental / Title regime
- **Seller:** Capacity and title warranties subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties, "for administrative simplicity."
- **Buyer wants:** Separate regime with a 100% cap, at least six years, outside the general basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. Title and capacity must sit in their own regime. Merging them into the general regime removes the protection the playbook requires.

### SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out
- **Seller:** Limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to "all Claims of any nature" (cl 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5). No fraud carve-out appears.
- **Buyer wants:** Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. No one may waive this.
- **Recommendation:** Reject and insert the carve-out. The Seller's "any nature" wording would bar claims for fraud, which is non-negotiable.

### SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope
- **Seller:** General disclosure of the whole data room (DD-002 to DD-012), the Accounts, statutory registers and public records (Disclosure Letter 1.1 and 1.2; Schedule 7).
- **Buyer wants:** Specific fair disclosure only. Reject whole-data-room, public-register and prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- **Recommendation:** Reject 1.1, 1.2 and Schedule 7 in their current form. General deemed disclosure would silently defeat the warranties.

### SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier
- **Seller:** No Buyer claim for any matter the Buyer or its advisers knew of, including anything discoverable from the data room or public records (cl 8.3).
- **Buyer wants:** Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions deleted. Any knowledge qualifier must name Seller knowledge persons and require reasonable enquiry. It must never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.
- **Recommendation:** Delete cl 8.3. "Discoverable from the data room" is a constructive-knowledge standard that the playbook rejects.

### SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent
- **Seller:** Reasonable endeavours. Consent treated as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent (cl 3 / 6.3). The disclosure confirms no final written consent or evidence of satisfied conditions exists (DD-002 clause 11.2 and 11.3; ~AUD 3.6m, ~30% of FY26 revenue).
- **Buyer wants:** Effective consent and evidence that its conditions are satisfied before Completion. Not consent-on-delivery. Reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient for a material customer consent.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. Make an effective Bluefen consent, with evidence of satisfied conditions, a condition precedent to Completion.

### SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility
- **Seller:** Approximately AUD 3.2m outstanding, to be addressed by a release provided after Completion (cl 2 / 7). The disclosure confirms the facility has not been repaid and no discharge is included (DD-003 clauses 8.1 and 9.2).
- **Buyer wants:** Current payout figure, direct repayment from Completion funds, and effective security releases. Any post-completion release requires an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost's approval.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the post-completion release. Require payout from Completion funds with effective releases at Completion. Escalate to Amelia Frost if any post-completion release is still proposed.

### SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses
- **Seller:** The AUD 420,000 closing bonuses (DD-005) are "a matter for the Seller" and not itemised in the funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.
- **Buyer wants:** AUD 420,000 plus triggered on-costs shown as a specific funds-flow line item, or seller-funded. The funds flow must not silently exclude them.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the exclusion. Require a specific line item, or Seller funding, for the bonuses and quantified on-costs.

### SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity
- **Seller:** Indemnity limited to the specific SOW3 payment (cl 11.1), described as adequate. The AUD 180,000 open amount (DD-010) is not independently verified.
- **Buyer wants:** Broadened indemnity, preserving the SOW3 cure (cl 7.3 of DD-004). The AUD 180,000 is neither accepted nor rejected as owed, pending verification.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the narrow indemnity and mark up to a broader one. Require independent verification of the AUD 180,000 and of payment status before settling the amount.

### SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident (DD-006)
- **Seller:** A "preliminary operational matter, not expected to be material." The disclosure does not characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.
- **Buyer wants:** Assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand in either direction. Preserve logs, investigate, and require updates.
- **Recommendation:** Do not accept the "not material" conclusion. Require log preservation, a completed investigation with regular updates, and confirmation of notification obligations. I would also propose a specific indemnity as a mark-up option. That is my suggestion, not a stated playbook position.

### SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals
- **Seller:** Three renewals totalling AUD 330,000 (3 × AUD 110,000) are ordinary-course operating costs. The disclosure does not say whether they are unavoidable, terminable or accrued.
- **Buyer wants:** Assessment of the renewals. No automatic Debt classification and no price deduction.
- **Recommendation:** Accept the assessment process, not the characterisation. Review terms, termination rights and accrual status before concluding either way. Do not reclassify as Debt or deduct from price on the Seller's say-so.

### SPA-N-014: Category separation
- **Seller:** Tax and IP "settled under the general regime above." Title, Fundamental and general claims are run through the same caps, time limits and reliance provisions.
- **Buyer wants:** Title, Tax, IP, payment and covenant categories kept separate. No hidden general-regime override.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. Every category keeps its own regime, and the general regime must not override any of them.

### SPA-N-015: Title verification
- **Seller:** Title to 100% of shares evidenced by the share register at DD-012. The disclosure confirms this is the source relied on, not independent verification.
- **Buyer wants:** Independent evidence of title, ownership, encumbrances and authority. DD-012 is a supplied internal source, not independent proof.
- **Recommendation:** Reject DD-012 as sufficient. Obtain independent evidence, such as a current ASIC company extract and searches for encumbrances, and verify authority before signing.

### SPA-N-016: Tax / IP open terms
- **Seller:** Tax and IP warranty positions "settled under the general regime above."
- **Buyer wants:** Tax and IP terms remain open. Assume no unlimited liability and no resolution.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the settlement claim and keep these terms open. Do not accept that they fall under the general regime.

---

### Escalations requiring Amelia Frost's written approval
1. Any general cap below 25% (the Seller's 20% / AUD 4.8m). None has been given.
2. Any general claims period below 24 months (the Seller's 18 months). None has been given.
3. Any post-completion Riverlark release (requires an irrevocable undertaking plus her approval).
